item.title: Magnetic nanocomposites could help shrink the components that power computer chips
item.description: When you think about making computer chips better, you probably think about transistors. My colleagues and I focused on a less visible part of the problem: the components that deliver power to those transistors. A chip needs more than electricity. It needs electricity supplied at the right voltage, with fluctuations kept under control. Making the hardware that does this smaller is an important challenge—and one that led my colleagues and me to build tiny magnetic devices called stripline microinductors. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Unos investigadores han decidido ponerle patas a un teléfono móvil y el resultado ha sido un robot que camina
item.description: En muchos cajones hay móviles que no volveremos a utilizar como teléfonos. Los guardamos después de estrenar otro, quizá por si algún día hacen falta, y ahí se quedan aunque sigan teniendo una cámara , un procesador, sensores de movimiento y conexión inalámbrica. Nos hemos acostumbrado a medir su utilidad por lo bien que sirven para llamar, hacer fotos o utilizar aplicaciones, pero esos componentes no desaparecen cuando dejamos de llevarlos encima. Y eso plantea una posibilidad bastante más interesante que darles una segunda vida como teléfono de repuesto. En la Universidad de California en… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Ask HN: Which TV do you recommend for privacy?
item.description: I haven’t owned a TV in years and would like one that respects my privacy. Are there any TV’s which do this well? I am looking for something in the 60”to 80”range and would like a 4k display with at least 60hz display. I don’t mind paying a premium. I have heard good things about Apple TV as a better alternative to most smart TV native apps. Would some TV’s pair better with this than others for privacy? I don’t want the TV doing anything other than being the display for Apple TV. I am curious what success others have had.
